title: Russian opposition politician Ilya Yashin cancels trip to Armenia for the final day of Russia’s State Duma elections after being warned of what he called a ‘physical threat’ — Meduza
text:
Opposition politician Ilya Yashin said he has called off a trip to Yerevan after being warned of “risks” tied to visiting Armenia.

Yashin, who is in the United States, had planned to travel to Yerevan and go to a polling station on September 20 to join “a big antiwar line,” and to meet with antiwar Russians.

“But while I was in Washington, I was warned about certain risks connected to my trip to Armenia. I can’t go into details, but this involves a physical threat. Unfortunately, I can’t ignore that information, and I have to follow security protocols. So the trip to Armenia is being postponed, and my participation in the events planned there is canceled,” Yashin said on his Telegram channel.

He still plans to take part in the “Noon for a Peaceful Russia” protest, he said. At noon on September 20, he intends to go to the polling station near the Russian Embassy in New York.

Yashin and several other opposition figures proposed staging the “Noon for a Peaceful Russia” protest on September 20, the final day of voting in the State Duma elections. They called on “everyone who disagrees with the policies Putin is pursuing” to cast their ballots that day at exactly noon.
